text: Old school attendance registers are pretty useful for reconstructing daily life. Historians use them to figure out who was there and who wasn't and how often, and sometimes why they missed. This helps you infer things like seasonal work demands, illness, bad weather, poverty or family stuff, migration, local emergencies. So you can see patterns by gender, age, neighborhood, social class. And how education fitted into work and household routines and community expectations. Across many years, you get changes in schooling habits and public health. But the thing is the registers only record what the school chose to note. They don't really go into what the kids experienced. Absences get misreported or are incomplete and teachers might have their own assumptions. So they're really only useful when you compare them to other sources.
